The claim petition has been filed by the petitioner against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 09.10.2022.
2.

The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
That on 09.10.2022 at about 6.15 p.m., while the petitioner and his friend were walking on Marasandra - Nellukunte Road, near Basava Bricks, Hesaraghatta Hobli,
Yelahanka Taluk, at that time, the rider of the Motor cycle Engine bearing No.DKXCMF20444 and Chasis bearing No.MD2A13EX2MCF36748 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the SCCH-10 petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and he was shifted to the hospital and taken inpatient treatment.
He has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses.

Further contended that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 27 years,
he was doing Coolie work and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
On account of the injuries sustained in the accident, he could not do his work as he was doing earlier, he became permanently disabled and put to irreparable loss of income.
Further, the alleged accident had taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending Motor cycle.
The respondent No.1 being owner and the respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the present petition.
3. Despite service of notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the Court, remained absent and placed exparte.
In pursuance to the notice, the respondent No.2 has SCCH-10 appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement.

4. The brief contentions of the respondent No.2 (insurer) are as under:
The respondent No.2 being insurer of offending vehicle has contended that, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable.
Further, the respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the offending motor cycle.

Further contended that, the jurisdictional police have filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s. 181 of Motor Vehicles Act as he was riding the motor cycle without possessing valid and effective driving Sunil Kumar vs Madhu on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15398012/
2 licence as on the date of accident.

The respondent No.2 has denied the accident,
manner in which the accident took place and rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending Motor cycle as well as its involvement in the alleged accident and also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Further denied the injuries sustained by the petitioner in SCCH-10 the alleged accident, treatment taken for those injuries, medical expenses incurred and permanent disability suffered by him.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
On these grounds, respondent No.2 prayed for dismissal of the claim petition against it.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of Pulsar Chasis No.MD2A13EX2MCF36748 by its rider,
in RTA that took place on 09.10.2022 at about 6.15 p.m. on Marasandra - Nellukunte Road, Near Basava Bricks, Hesaragatta Hobli, Yelahanka Taluk, Bengaluru ?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award?
6. The petitioner, in order to prove his case examined himself as PW-1 and examined the doctor as PW-2 and in all got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.
The respondent SCCH-10 No.2 examined its official as RW-1 and got marked documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3.
7. Heard the arguments.
Perused the materials available on record.

8. My findings to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order, for the following :
R E A S O N S 9. ISSUE No.1:
The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with respect to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.
Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR No.0250/2022 of Rajanukunte PS and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, it reveal that I.O. has registered a case Sunil Kumar vs Madhu on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15398012/
3 against the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Engine No.DKXCMF20444 for the commission of offence punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of charge sheet filed by the SCCH-10 Rajanukunte PS.

On perusal of Ex.P.5, it reveals that, after investigation the police have filed charge sheet against one Mr. Madhu,
who is none other than the respondent No.1/ rider cum owner of offending Motor cycle for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 338 R/w Section 181 of Motor Vehicles Act.
10.
Further, as per wound certificate i.e. Ex.P.4 produced by petitioner and Ex.P.5 discharge summary, it appears that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.

On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle and petitioner has sustained injuries in the said accident.

11. As discussed supra, the IO after investigation has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending motor cycle showing him as an accused in the said case and as per the police records, it reveal that the rider of the offending vehicle was riding the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and SCCH-10 has caused the accident.
12. Besides, it is settled principles of law that, in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required

. This view is supported by the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.

sentences.text: 13. Thus, by considering the present facts of the case and the materials placed on record, I am of the opinion that, the accident in question had occurred due to the negligent and rash riding of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Chasis No.MD2A13EX2MCF36748.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE No.2:-
The petitioner contended that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.

He further SCCH-10 stated that, after the accident, he was shifted to Bowring hospital, Bengaluru and after taking one week inpatient treatment for further treatment he was shifted to MGM Medical hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took inpatient treatment for one week.

15. Before proceeding to discuss this issue, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2011(1) S.C.C page 343 in the case of Rajkumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar.
In para No.5 of the judgment, Hon'ble Apex Court has mentioned the heads under which compensation is to be awarded in personal injury cases.
I reproduce the same hereunder for convenience.
The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following;
Pecuniary damages (special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, Medicines, transportation, nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
Future Medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (general damages) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
Loss of amenities (and / or loss of prospects of marriage) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
Keeping in view the law declared in the aforementioned decision, I have carefully perused the entire materials placed on record.
The wound certificate of the petitioner has been marked as Ex.P.4.

As per the wound certificate, wherein it reveals that swelling seen on the right leg, referred to orthopaedic, according to Bowring hospital orthopaedics, type-3 bone open fracture middle to distal 1/3rd of right leg and doctor opined that, the said injury is SCCH-10 grievous in nature.

16. In this case, the discharge summary produced by the petitioner as per Ex.P.6 reveals that, the petitioner for further treatment admitted to MGM Medical hospital, Bengaluru on 06.07.2024 with complaint of pain in right lower limb and difficulty in walking and in the said hospital, he was given surgical treatment, closed reduction internal fixation tibia intra-medulery inter locking nail under spinal and epidural anesthesia on 26.09.2023.
17.
Ex.P.8 are the medical bills amounting to Rs.18,156/- and Ex.P.9 are the medical prescriptions.
The medical bills produced by the petitioner appears to be genuine.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for actual medical bills and same is rounded off to Rs.18,200/- under the head of Medical expenses.
18. As per the medical documents it appear that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and he is suffering from physical disability.
By considering the nature of injury, SCCH-10 the petitioner might have suffered pain and agony.
Considering the age of the petitioner, I am of the opinion that if Rs.40,000/- is awarded towards pain and sufferings it would be just.
If Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards nourishment and diet food it would be just.

sentences.text: The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury he has undergone surgery and suffering from permanent disability.
He has further stated that, due to the disability he has lost his earning capacity.
In order to establish the disability, the doctor was examined before the Court as PW2.
PW-2 during his evidence has deposed that, the petitioner has sustained right leg compound fracture of tibia and fibula.
Further, on examination, the petitioner has wasting of the right thigh and calf muscles, restricted knee and ankle movements.
X-ray of right leg shows united fracture with implant in situ.
Further, the petitioner has suffered physical impairment disability of 42% to right lower limb and 14% to the whole body.
Though the PW-2 doctor was cross-examined by the counsel for the respondent No.2, SCCH-10 nothing was elicited from the mouth of the witness to disprove his evidence.
20. According to the petitioner, he was aged about 27 years at the time of accident and he was doing Coolie work and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration.

At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2023(4)
KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another.

entities.text: Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above decision the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru (KSLSA in short).

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The KSLSA, Bengaluru as per letter dated 26.02.2022 - 01/NLA/2022/550/2022 has circulated the notional income chart prepared by them.
As per the said notional income chart, the income for the year 2022 is fixed as Rs.15,500/-

Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court and the letter of KSLSA and also in the SCCH-10 absence of proof of income, this Court is of the opinion that, if the notional income is taken into consideration for assessing the income of the petitioner would be just and proper.
The accident was occurred on 09.10.2022.
Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.15,500/- as monthly income of the petitioner.
21. On perusal of the medical documents and medical evidence it is crystal clear that, the petitioner cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier.
Hence, the disability of the petitioner will definitely come in the way of the petitioner in his future earnings.
22. As per the doctor, the whole body disability is approximately 14%.
It is settled principles that all permanent disabilities arising out of injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability.

Even though the doctor has opined 14% permanent disability to the whole SCCH-10 body,
considering the nature of work of the petitioner and considering the disability, I assess the petitioner's loss of future earning capacity as 12%.
23. To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.7.
As per Ex.P.7, the date of birth of petitioner is shown as 01.01.1997.
The accident was occurred on 09.10.2022.

Hence,
the age of the petitioner is considered as 25 years at the time of accident and multiplier applicable for his age is 18.
The loss of future earning capacity is assessed as 12%.
The annual income is assessed Rs.1,86,000/-(Rs.15,500 x 12).
Therefore, the loss of future income would be Rs.1,86,000/-(annual income) X 18 (multiplier) X 12% = Rs.4,01,760/-.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future income of Rs.4,01,760/-.

sentences.text: The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury and disability he is unable to do any physical strain works and the disability is coming in the way of his day today activities and avocation.
Hence, considering the injuries SCCH-10 suffered, this Court is of the opinion that, due to disability, the petitioner must forego some comforts in his life.
Hence, I conclude that if Rs.25,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities it would be just.
doctor in his evidence has stated that, the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.60,000/-.
Admittedly, the petitioner has not produced any estimation for removal of implants.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, if Rs.25,000/- is awarded towards future medical expenses it will be just and this amount shall not carry any future interest.

26. Thus, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads;
Sl.
 Heads Compensation No.
1) Medical expenses Rs. 18,200 /-
2) Pain and sufferings Rs. 40,000/-
3) Nourishment and diet food Rs. 15,000 /-
4) Loss of Future earning Rs. 4,01,760/-
 SCCH-10  capacity due to permanent  disability 5) Loss of amenities Rs. 25,000 /-
6) Future Medical expenses Rs. 25,000/-
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,24,960/-.
27. REGARDING LIABILITY:

As discussed supra, this Court has arrived at the conclusion that, the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Engine No.DKXCMF20444 and Chasis No.MD2A13EX2MCF36748.

The respondent No.1 has insured the vehicle with respondent No.2, as such,
respondent No.2 has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Admittedly, the Insurance Policy was in force on the date of accident.

28. The respondent No.2 in the written statement has specifically contended that, at the time of accident the charge sheeted rider had no valid and effective driving SCCH-10 licence to ride the offending motor cycle and hence the insured/owner of the offending Motor cycle has violated the terms and conditions of the policy and hence, the insurance company is not liable to pay any Sunil Kumar vs Madhu on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15398012/
7 compensation.

29. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 while canvassing the arguments has drawn my attention towards Ex.P.5 Charge sheet and submitted that, on the date of accident the rider of the offending motor cycle had no valid driving licence and hence, I.O has invoked Section 181 of Motor Vehicles Act and hence, submitted that, the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation for the fundamental breach of policy condition.
30. In the instant case, as per the police records, the rider of the offending motor cycle had no valid driving licence on the date of accident.

Therefore, this Court is the opinion that, respondent No.1 who is the rider/owner of the offending vehicle was riding the motor cycle without having valid driving licence and has committed fundamental breach of policy condition.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the SCCH-10 owner of the vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

31. The counsel for the petitioner has argued that, the petitioner is third party victim and though there is violation of policy condition if any, the insurance company has to satisfy the award amount and can recover the same from the owner.

32. It has been held by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in New India Assurance Co., Ltd., v/s Yallavva W/o Yamanappa Dharnakeri in M.F.A. No. 30131 OF 2010 (MV-I) dated 12 May, 2020 that,
ii) The Insurer is liable to pay the third party and recover from the insured even if there is breach of any condition recognized under Section 149(2), even if it is a fundamental breach (that is breach of condition which is the cause for the accident) and the insurer proves the said breach in view of the mandate under Section 149(1) of the Act."

entities.text: New India Assurance Co., Ltd., v/s Yallavva W/o Yamanappa Dharnakeri
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
33. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 would submit that, after the replacement of Section 149 of the SCCH-10 Motor Vehicles Act 1988 by Section 150 of Amendment Act 2019, the liability of the insurer to pay and its right to recover the amount from the owner has been taken away and hence, in the instant case, since the accident occurred after the said amendment, the Court cannot direct to pay compensation to the insurance company and to recover it from the owner.
34.
In the instant case, though there is a violation of policy condition, the respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and same was in force on the date of accident.
The amendment to Section 149 of the Act will not take away the liability of the insurer to pay the claimants who being the third party.

Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the insurer shall continue to indemnify the owner's risk in relation to the accident taking place after 01.04.2022 as Motor Vehicles Act is a Benevolent Legislation, the claimants cannot be deprived of the compensation.

Therefore, in view of the valid insurance policy and indemnity between the respondents insured and SCCH-10 insurer and in view of the above principles, at the first instance,
the insurer i.e. respondent No.2 has to pay the award amount of Rs.5,24,960/- to the petitioner with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.

Accordingly, I answer the Sunil Kumar vs Madhu on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15398012/
8 issue No.2
partly in the Affirmative.
35. Issue No.3:

In view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,24,960/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
The respondent No.2 being insurer is directed to deposit the entire compensation SCCH-10 amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
The respondent No.2 / insurance company is at liberty to recover the compensation amount from the owner/ respondent No.1 in accordance with law.

Out of the award amount, 25% of the award amount shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 2 years in any nationalized bank of petitioner's choice and balance amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner through NEFT / RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.
